newsitem.title: MEXICO: Coca-Cola Femsa details Q4, 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola Femsa details Q4, 1996 results.

text.p: Coca-Cola Femsa, a bottling joint venture with operations in Mexico and Argentina, reported higher sales volume and net profits in both territories in the fourth quarter.

The company, known as KOF, said that in Mexico sales rose 12.1 percent from the fourth quarter of 1995 to 74 million unit cases, while in Argentina sales volume rose 19.7 percent to 30.4 million unit cases, including 3.3 million unit cases sold in the San Isidro territory which was fully acquired in the first quarter of 1996.
Discounting the San Isidro territory, it said sales volume in Argentina grew 8.6 percent.
Net sales for KOF in Mexican operations grew 9.8 percent to 1.217 billion pesos, despite an average price per unit case reduction of two percent.
Gross profit was 582 million, up 12.4 percent from the fourth quarter of 1995, while gross margin increased to 47.8 percent from 46.8 percent.

"These increases were mainly due to a greater fixed-cost absorption generated through increased sales volumes and by a real decrease in the unit price of certain raw materials, as well as efficiencies derived from recent investments," KOF said.

Operating income for KOF's Mexico operations rose 35.4 percent to 206.1 million pesos in the fourth quarter compared to the same period a year before, giving an operating margin of 16.9 percent, up 3.2 percentage points.
In Buenos Aires, net sales rose 14.9 percent to 122 million Argentine pesos while cost of goods sold grew five percent to 69 million Argentine pesos.
Operating income rose to 14.6 million Argentine pesos from 1.5 million in the fourth quarter of 1995.

In the company's consolidated results, 1995 figures for the Argentine operation were restated taking into account Argentine 1996 inflation and converted into Mexican pesos at 7.865 Mexican pesos per Argentine peso.

"Due to the operating improvement of KOF's businesses, consolidated operating income (after the increased goodwill amortisation charges attributable to the San Isidro territory) increased 99.4 percent during the fourth quarter to 310 million pesos," KOF said.

Consolidated operating margin reached 14.2 percent, up 6.2 percentage points, while consolidated EBITDA (operating income plus depreciation, amortisation and other non-cash items including returnable bottle breakage) grew 78.4 percent to 476.2 million pesos.
Integral financing cost fell to 46.4 million pesos from 77.6 million in the fourth quarter of 1995.
The company said majority net earnings per share rose 286.3 percent to 0.55 pesos, or $0.70 per ADR.

In all of 1996, consolidated net sales rose 6.1 percent from 1995 to 7.598 billion pesos while operating profit rose 24.3 percent to 641.3 million. KOF said majority net earnings per share rose to 1.05 pesos, or $1.33 per ADR.

KOF said its Buenos Aires arm had bought a 44.2 percent stake in can maker Complejo Industrial Can SA in December 1996 for $4.6 million and believed the purchase would lower can purchase costs and improve gross margin. ($1 = 7.75 Mexican pesos)
